identity.name: link_wsib
identity.description: Matches WSIB registry entries to builder entities via a 3-tier bulk SQL cascade (exact trade name 0.95, exact legal name 0.90, pg_trgm fuzzy 0.60) and writes wsib_registry.linked_entity_id/match_confidence/matched_at plus entities.is_wsib_registered (exact tiers only, LW-D19 2026-08-29 — a tier-3/fuzzy link never confers registration) and the fill-only contact columns, per tier, plus an unconditional per-run is_wsib_registered self-heal correction, in one step-scoped transaction.

why_lock.text: Lock 94 is not the spec number (this step's primary governing spec is 46). It was assigned by the c1ef0b73 advisory-lock retrofit and is recorded in src/tests/pipeline-advisory-lock.infra.test.ts's registry ('scripts/link-wsib.js': 94) — kept textually per §5.4 so that registry stays green across the conversion.

guard_why.text: O4 row 6 (operator D3(a), registry-truth fold 16 row 1 (c)): compare-and-set on the OLD link. Each keyed row is updated only while (linked_entity_id, match_confidence) IS NOT DISTINCT FROM the (old entity, old confidence) the read-only derivation saw, AND IS DISTINCT FROM the new link (buildApplyLinksSql), so a row changed since the derivation, or a re-run over an applied difference, writes 0 rows. matched_at is never in a guard (LG-9: a run-clock stamp).

write_discipline.scope: the derivation's set + move rows, keyed `w.id = u.id` via `unnest($2..$6)` (buildApplyLinksSql)

why.text: LG-11 (finding 3, Fold A/B, 2026-08-28). Neither pre-existing write.js executor fits: executeSetBasedClear only writes a DECLARED CONSTANT; executeUpsertBatch is ALWAYS INSERT-capable (ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE), and wsib_registry rows may only ever be CREATED by load-wsib.js — an accidental INSERT here would violate that ownership boundary worse than a missed match. write.executeSetBasedJoinUpdate refuses any statement containing INSERT INTO or ON CONFLICT at execution time (checked on the actual SQL text, not a class label).

write_discipline.scope: id IN (SELECT linked_entity_id FROM wsib_registry WHERE match_confidence IN ($1, $2)) AND is_wsib_registered = false

why.text: G-9: runs immediately after EACH tier's own wsib_registry UPDATE — $1/$2 are ALWAYS the two EXACT tiers' resolved confidences (`exactTierConfidences`), never whichever tier's own pass is currently running (write.executeSetBasedClear's existing scopeParams binding, no write.js change needed). LW-D19 (2026-08-29 operator ruling): `is_wsib_registered` is a product-visible registration claim; the fuzzy tier (0.60, 32-47% precision by fixed-rule sample, assessment §8d) no longer confers it — restricting the scope to the closed 2-value exact set is Spec 124 §7 rung (a); running the SAME statement, with the SAME params, on the fuzzy tier's own pass rather than branching it out is rung (b) ('no second code path') — a fuzzy-only match is a genuine no-op here, not a skipped call.

guard_why.text: 647d0935's copyContacts NULLIF-guard, ported verbatim: only fills a currently-empty contact field, never overwrites (Spec 46 §2 Contact Flow, G-15). The set clause's right-hand sides are subquery-aggregated per entity, not a declared constant, so this target uses the same LG-11 executor as the wsib join-update rather than set_based_scoped's constant-only codegen.

write_discipline.scope: w_agg.linked_entity_id = e.id AND wsib_registry.match_confidence = $1, aggregated per tier (fill-only via NULLIF, never overwrite)

why.text: Once a contact field is filled, the NULLIF(...) IS NULL guard excludes the row from ever matching again — a re-run over an unchanged corpus changes 0 rows, same idempotence class as the wsib_registry join-update.

guard_why.text: Only touches a row still carrying a link (IS DISTINCT FROM null), and the keyed scope already compares each row's (id, linked_entity_id, match_confidence) against the old link the derivation saw, so a row re-linked since then, or an already-NULLed row on a re-run, changes 0 rows. Enforced by write.js's set-based guard-clause codegen, not by the scope predicate alone.

why.text: LG-16, re-scoped by O4 row 6 (operator D1(a)/D3(a)): a keyed UPDATE-to-NULL of the links that VANISHED from the read-only derivation, of ANY tier (the former tier-3-only scope-wide retraction and its asymmetry are gone), bound $1 = vanished ids, $2 = old entity ids, $3 = old confidences. Never a DELETE: wsib_registry ROWS are load-wsib.js's exclusive territory, and retracting a LINK must never retract the ROW. Declared under its own class so every place this step retracts is findable by the class name, and the LG-16 fence lock asserts 'never DELETE' against the generated SQL.

write_discipline.scope: is_wsib_registered = true AND id NOT IN (SELECT linked_entity_id FROM wsib_registry WHERE match_confidence IN ($1, $2))

why.text: LW-D19 (2026-08-29 operator ruling, Spec 124 §7 rung (c)). The is_wsib_registered SELF-HEAL correction: runs ONCE per invocation, UNCONDITIONAL of mode — never gated to mode "full" like A-7/LG-16's retraction (writes[3]) above, because this is not a repair of wsib_registry's links, it is keeping a DERIVED entities column honest every run. The fill-true target (writes[1]) only ever transitions false→true (scope 'AND is_wsib_registered = false'); this target is the ONLY mechanism that ever transitions an entity back to false when its registration claim has no exact-tier link backing it — together they express 'is_wsib_registered ≡ EXISTS an exact-tier link', both directions, self-healing (no one-off FULL correction script needed — the simplest closed form per the operator's own framing). Same declared set_based_scoped/is_distinct_from shape as writes[1], the opposite constant and scope — a re-run over an already-corrected corpus changes 0 rows.

invalidates.when: an entity is added, renamed or removed, a wsib_registry row's normalized names change, or the fuzzy threshold or a tier confidence changes. O4 row 6 (registry-truth folds 14 + 16, operator D1-D5 (a)): link_wsib re-derives the best link of every wsib_registry row on every run (staleness.mode_select "none") in a read-only derivation and writes only the difference (compare-and-set writes[0] for set and move rows, keyed UPDATE-to-NULL writes[3] for vanished links), so no separate invalidator is needed. O4 row 3 retired the former entities.is_wsib_registered row (P1-C6 source #5 landed, 6de9d6a0).

why.text: O4 row 6 (LW-D23): the statement inventory per real run is FIXED, one mode, always issued (empty arrays write 0): a READ ONLY transaction {set_config, diff SELECT} (reads), then one write transaction of 6 DISTINCT statements (8 executions): W-set (writes[0]), W-vanish (writes[3]), the contacts reverse clear, the entities flag (writes[1]) x1 (was x3), the self-heal correction (writes[4]) x1, and copyContacts (writes[2]) — ONE statement executed x3 (per tier, parameterized by the tier's confidence). #44 (c) counts distinct statements (trace fingerprints), so the count is 6 (FLEET-2 §5.8, measured on the fleet #2 forced trace). The former incremental 10 / full 13 per-mode rows collapse into one (closes the C7-2 gap).

on_prior_run_error_why.text: A failed prior-run read degrades this step to 'no baseline' — the config_version diff and the upstream_ledger count both fail-safe to CHANGED (never SKIP) on an absent baseline, so warn_row's cost is a real run rather than a silently stale gate, unlike an ingest loader whose baseline gates a destructive departure DELETE.

why.text: Tier 3's entire predicate is pg_trgm similarity() over GIN trigram indexes (measured live: v1.6, present). Without it the fuzzy tier cannot run at all — there is no second algorithm to fall back to (unlike link_massing's now-retired JS path).

The GIN trigram index Tier 3's trade_name_normalized comparison seeks. Without it the % operator degrades to a sequential scan over 121,116 rows per batch — the same class of failure tasks/lessons.md records for link_massing's spatial GiST indexes.
The GIN trigram index for legal_name_normalized — the other half of Tier 3's UNION ALL split (647d0935, avoiding the ~394M-row nested loop the OR-joined version produced).
Measured live: relrowsecurity=true, 0 policies. Under any role that does not bypass RLS every tier's UPDATE affects 0 rows with NO error — indistinguishable from an unchanged corpus.
Same class, the other side of the join: entities also carries RLS enabled.

on_check_error_why.text: Every check reads a value the library already measured — a check that throws is a library defect, not an upstream condition. It must redden the run, not drop its row.

expect.reports: the resolved mode and the ledger gated-skip decision

why.text: LG-15's gated-skip and A-8's tri-state mode, on the record — visible even on a gated skip (the same class as link_massing's full_mode_gate row).

LINK_WSIB_FORCE_FULL left standing bypasses the ledger-gated skip on every subsequent run (since O4 row 6 it no longer changes the mode — every run is a full rescan). Reported (not gated) so a forgotten override is discoverable by reading the audit table.

expect.of: (moves + vanishes) over the wsib_registry rows linked at run start (linked_start), a FRACTION

why.text: O4 row 6 mass guard (operator D2(a), registry-truth fold 16 row 1 (b)). The read-only derivation has no diff cap, so a bad corpus or a mis-set confidence could move or NULL most stored links in one run. Scored pre_write on the derivation's own counts, before any write; the value is a FRACTION (heritage_mass_delete_pct precedent), default 0.10. LINK_WSIB_ACCEPT_MASS_RELINK=1 lets the run write and never suppresses the FAIL row. Steady state measured 0 moves / 0 vanishes (2026-10-03, local dev DB, READ ONLY).

order_guarantee.guarantee: link_wsib must abort BEFORE any link write whenever the moved + vanished links exceed the configured fraction of the links held at run start, unless LINK_WSIB_ACCEPT_MASS_RELINK accepts it.
order_guarantee.anchor: 60:stops the write; `LINK_WSIB_ACCEPT_MASS_RELINK=1` lets it through and the FAIL row stays

expect.of: entities with at least one linked wsib_registry row (entities.is_wsib_registered = true) / total entities

why.text: LW-D1, the P4 violation this pilot closes: pre-conversion the floor was the bare literal 5 in `linkRate >= 5 ? PASS : WARN`. Reported as the RATE itself (not the unlinked complement, unlike link_massing's link_rate — T2's config value IS the floor, so a `pct >=` form is the correctly-shaped comparison; `pct <=` would compare the wrong direction). LW-D18 (2026-08-29) RE-RULED the denominator from wsib_registry ROWS to ENTITIES: the row-based ratio let a single magnet entity's hundreds of contaminated rows inflate the numerator without representing hundreds of genuinely-covered builders — the ratio an operator actually wants is "what share of our builder pool has a WSIB record at all," i.e. `entities.is_wsib_registered = true` count over total entities (the SAME flag `registered_entities_with_zero_links` already reads). LW-D19 (2026-08-29) narrowed WHAT `is_wsib_registered` means (exact tiers only, no longer any tier) without touching this check's shape: measured live post-LW-D19, entities.is_wsib_registered fell from 551 to 301 (the exact-tier-linked population) / 3,948 total = 7.62%, still comfortably above the 5% floor — see the LW-D19 correction table in the assessment report for the exact before/after. Default kept at 5. R-H (Spec 124 Rule 10 addendum): a standing non-zero population is WARN with a declared, machine-observable retighten condition, never FAIL, never INFO-by-taste. RETIGHTEN CONDITION: if the entity-level rate rises meaningfully above the ~7.6% LW-D19 baseline (e.g. from a corpus-wide re-repair or a further precision fix), review raising `link_wsib_link_rate_warn_pct` above 5 to keep the floor meaningful.

expect.of: the max wsib_registry rows linked to any single entity

why.text: T6, new this pilot (Fold A, Reality-Check). Fires immediately on the known-bad population (171 magnet entities fan-in >= 10, worst MDK CONSTRUCTION at 2,118) — intended, not a defect (Fold B ACCEPTED ruling). A declared, machine-observable population this pilot surfaces rather than gates away. R-H (Spec 124 Rule 10 addendum): WARN with a declared, machine-observable retighten condition, never FAIL, never INFO-by-taste. RETIGHTEN CONDITION: the fan-in magnets are near-entirely tier-3 (fuzzy, 0.60-confidence) contamination — once A-7's tier-3 repair (LG-16) retracts the 61.9%-failing tier-3 links, `wsib_entity_fanin_max` should fall well below its current 2,118 (MDK CONSTRUCTION) and 1,404 (COLE CONTRACTING); at that point `link_wsib_entity_fanin_warn` (currently 20, deliberately loose so the check fires on the known-bad population rather than gating it away) should be reviewed for lowering toward a tighter bound that reflects genuinely healthy fan-in.

expect.of: the pct of Tier-3 (fuzzy, 0.60-confidence) links whose WSIB name and matched entity name share at least one non-generic (stopword-stripped, non-numeric) token

why.text: LW-D14 (2026-08-28), tightened LW-D18 (2026-08-29). `similarity() > threshold` + first-letter blocking (d704a447) is satisfiable by two UNRELATED companies that merely share a generic word ("* CONTRACTING", "* CONSTRUCTION") — the root cause of the magnet-entity fan-in contamination `entity_fanin_warn` (T6) surfaces. Measured live PRE-fix (LW-D14): 10.49% (840 of 8,009 tier-3 links share a genuine non-generic token; the rest share only a generic word or nothing). LW-D18: a 60-row random precision sample of the LW-D14-fixed tier-3 population measured only 15.0% confirmed-genuine (9/60; up to 25.0% counting 6 UNSURE) — 80% of the confirmed failures shared ONE of 15 more industry-generic words (GENERAL, RENOVATION(S), MANAGEMENT, DESIGN, BUILD, CUSTOM, HOME, IMPROVEMENT(S), BUILDING, ASSOCIATES, TOP, ALL, QUALITY) that were still treated as genuine signal, producing new post-fix magnet entities (e.g. ARC General Contracting ×4, I & R Renovations ×4). Widened the stopword list with those 15 words (same declared field, Rule 1). `buildFuzzyMatchSql`'s predicate now REQUIRES the same token-overlap rule this check measures (`tokenOverlapClause`, `scripts/lib/compute/link-wsib.js`), so a healthy corpus reads at or near 100% post-fix — FAIL (not WARN, R-H does not apply: this measures the write predicate's own correctness after the fix landed, never an expected-permanently-nonzero population), blocking:false (report loudly, do not halt — the SAME posture `link_rate_warn` uses). The stopword list is declared here (`expect.stopwords`), never a literal in compute (Rule 1) — `buildFuzzyMatchSql`/`buildCumulativeSql` both read it from this exact field via `tokenOverlapStopwords(descriptor)`.
Invariant, pinned by the golden captures (commit 5): a linked_entity_id with a NULL match_confidence or matched_at is a partial write the cascade's own paired columns should make impossible.
The written vocabulary is the three resolved tier confidences (T3/T4/T5) — no other value should ever reach the column.

expect.reports: rows with match_confidence in [0.50, 0.60) — the stats query's own dead bucket boundary

why.text: LW-D4, INCIDENTAL classification (PH-6): no code path ever writes a confidence in this range, so the pre-conversion stats query's 0.50 lower bound was always dead. Reported, not fixed — a declared limitation, not a defect.

Invariant, pinned by the golden captures. is_wsib_registered may only be true because a wsib_registry row links to this entity — a registered entity with zero links is the write ORDER breaking (G-9), or A-7's unflag cascade missing a row. LW-D19 (2026-08-29) narrowed WHAT counts as a qualifying link (exact tiers only) WITHOUT tightening this invariant's own predicate (deliberately kept as "a link of ANY tier", the pre-LW-D19 shape) — the strictly stronger invariant ("a link of an EXACT tier") is `is_wsib_registered_corrected`, below, whose non-zero violations value on this check would never fire while that one still can (an entity with only a fuzzy link has a link, satisfying THIS check, while failing the exact-tier one) — a genuine widen-then-narrow layering, not a duplicate.

expect.reports: entities this run's LW-D19 self-heal correction flipped from is_wsib_registered=true to false (no exact-tier link backing the claim)

why.text: LW-D19 (2026-08-29 operator ruling). The self-heal correction target's (writes[4]) own audit row, read from `ctx.matched.is_wsib_registered_corrected` — populated by `runCascadePhase`'s unconditional post-tier-loop correction pass (`scripts/lib/step/index.js`), never a literal. INFO, always present (the correction runs every real invocation, never gated to mode "full"). Expected: the historical gap (measured 551 → 301, the 250-row difference between `entities.is_wsib_registered = true` and `EXISTS an exact-tier link`, computed by SQL and cited BEFORE the run) is CLOSED as of this commit's live verification, but the verification run itself reported 0 here — a genuine, explained finding, not a silent gap: the verification used `LINK_WSIB_FORCE_FULL=1` (the only available gate-bypass), which resolves mode=full and therefore ALSO fires A-7/LG-16's pre-existing retraction, whose OWN unflag cascade (`buildEntitiesUnflagSql`, unconditional ‘NOT EXISTS any link’, unrelated to LW-D19) unflags every tier-3-only entity the MOMENT its link is retracted — before the tier loop relinks it and before this target's own pass ever runs. Both mechanisms reach the SAME 301 end state in mode=full, by construction, so this target's own counter reads 0 there. This target's DISTINCT, load-bearing contribution is INCREMENTAL-mode runs (the overwhelming majority in practice, A-8: full is a rare manual repair) — A-7 never fires there, so an incorrectly-true tier-3-only entity would never self-heal without this target. Proven directly and live (not mocked): a throwaway, rolled-back transaction against the real DB (this commit's WF3 session) manually set one genuinely tier-3-only entity `is_wsib_registered = true`, ran this exact target's generated SQL via the real `write.executeSetBasedClear`, and measured `rows changed = 1` (entity flips to false), while a control exact-tier-linked entity stayed `true` untouched, and a second identical pass changed 0 rows (idempotent) — then rolled back, leaving the live DB unmodified. See `docs/reports/defect-ledger.md` LW-D19 for the transcript.

why.text: Fold B BLOCKING a, re-scoped by O4 row 6 (operator D5(a)): counts entity contact fields cleared by the reverse clear over the derivation's MOVE + VANISH rows, keyed per (old entity, value) pairs; 0 in steady state (diff 0). Reused counter, no new one. Measured local exposure is 0 (PH-6: wsib_registry carries zero contact values on this DB); a limitations[] entry records that this does NOT bound cloud.

O4 row 6 (operator D2(a)): a deliberate mass relink (e.g. a confidence or threshold change the operator intends) is accepted for ONE run; the FAIL row is still written.

The schema's own drafters GUESSED a re-derivation from the OLD fused evidence-base labels without measuring. Measured this pilot (Fold A, Integration S1 + LG-11/LG-16 findings): the wsib_registry write is NOT expressible as class E (write_once_backfill) or G (set_based_scoped) — the SET clause's values are per-row JOIN results from a compute-authored matched CTE, which neither pre-existing class's codegen can generate. The correct classes are the two NEW ones this pilot adds: set_based_join_update (LG-11) and set_based_null_retract (LG-16). Spec 122 §1.4's text is stale and is corrected in the same commit (Spec Update step).

deviations.from: Spec 122 §1.2 checks[].limit's closed form set (pct <= only)

why.text: A genuine library gap, closed per Spec 124 §7 rung (d): link_wsib's link_rate_warn is a config-driven PERCENTAGE FLOOR (T2 = the floor value itself, not its complement — unlike link_massing's link_rate, where the config value coincidentally equals its own complement). limit_from_config's substitution is unconditional, so no existing form (pct <=, viol <=/==, pop >=) could express 'value >= the substituted config number' for a percentage. scripts/lib/step/verdict.js gains a symmetric pct >= form (evaluateLimit, PCT_RE) — every future step with a floor-shaped percentage check benefits, not just this one.

deviations.from: the pre-conversion script's dry-run simulation (5de41cc1: read-only COUNT queries mirroring tier1/tier2/tier3's wsib_registry match predicate only)

why.text: LW-D15. The CONVERSION SILENTLY DROPPED dry-run write-suppression entirely (the CRITICAL bug this deviation records the fix for: the converted step's `--dry-run` bypassed the ledger gate but then wrote for real, on EVERY converted LINK/MATCHER step, until this fix) — restoring it, this pilot's dry-run simulates ALL THREE per-tier write targets (wsib_registry match, entities flag-flip, entities contacts copy) via read-only count-query mirrors of each write's exact predicate (buildTierSql's *_count_sql siblings), not just the wsib_registry match 5de41cc1 covered. In mode=full it additionally simulates the LG-16 retraction (A-7, new this pilot, did not exist pre-conversion) using the already-read `priorContacts` row count — but runs the LG-16 tier-3 convergence loop (LW-D10, also new this pilot) exactly ONCE rather than looping to convergence: a dry-run issues zero writes, so the `linked_entity_id IS NULL` scope a later pass would re-query never shrinks, and a simulated 'pass 2' would just re-count pass 1's rows under a false `exhausted` label. Declared, not silently narrowed.

limitations.what: staleness.fingerprint_inputs' wsib_registry corpus signal is COUNT(*) only (upstream_ledger). G-19's fuller reading — trade_name_normalized is rewritten on EVERY load_wsib reload even when linked_entity_id is untouched, so an unchanged row count can still sit on a stale matching predicate — is not captured by a row-count-only signal. A MAX(last_seen_at)-based signal, or reading load_wsib's own source-version fingerprint directly, would close this; not built this commit.
limitations.measured: load-wsib.js ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET rewrites trade_name_normalized/last_seen_at on every reload but never linked_entity_id/match_confidence/matched_at (Fold C, confirmed by direct read, 2026-08-28)

limitations.what: The contacts reverse clear is provenance-by-equality, keyed per (old entity, value) pairs (O4 row 6, operator D5(a)): an entity's contact field is cleared only when its CURRENT value equals a value carried by a wsib row whose link this run MOVED or VANISHED, and only for diff rows (steady state 0). A contact that coincidentally matches such a row's value is cleared and re-copied on relink (a false positive, not a false negative — no contact is ever left dangling from a genuinely moved or vanished source).
limitations.measured: magnet_entities_with_any_contact = 7 of 171 magnets, but wsib_registry carries ZERO contact values locally (121,116 / 0 / 0) — the local 0 exposure does NOT bound cloud, which may carry Serper-enriched wsib_registry contact fields; re-run both queries against cloud before any cloud FULL run (PH-6, commit 4)

limitations.what: The [0.50, 0.60) match_confidence stats bucket boundary (a display-only artifact of the pre-conversion final-stats query) is DEAD — no code path writes a confidence in that range, since the three tiers write exactly 0.95/0.90/0.60. PINNED (Spec 123 §3.1), not fixed: nothing downstream reads or asserts on the boundary specifically.
limitations.measured: 0 rows with match_confidence in [0.50, 0.60) (golden capture invariant wsib_dead_bucket_050_060_count = 0, commit 5)

limitations.what: LW-D15, re-scoped by O4 row 6: a `--dry-run` invocation runs the read-only derivation and reports its set / move / vanish counts exactly, but issues no write. Its `contacts_cleared` is reported as 0, and the flag / correction / contacts counts are mirrors over the CURRENT links (they do not see the diff), so a dry-run preview of those three counters can differ from the real run that follows.

recovery.reset: TRUNCATE is never correct for wsib_registry (load-wsib.js owns row lifecycle) or entities. Re-run the step: since O4 row 6 (staleness.mode_select none) every run re-derives every wsib_registry row's best link and applies only the difference, so a plain re-run IS the repair. LINK_WSIB_FORCE_FULL=1 only bypasses the ledger-gated skip; it no longer changes the mode.

why.text: The normal outcome: the ledger gate did not skip, mode resolved incremental, the cascade ran.
Every real run since O4 row 6 (staleness.mode_select "none"): the read-only derivation ran over every wsib_registry row and only the difference was written.
A WARN row stands (link_rate_warn or entity_fanin_warn) and nothing FAILED. The run completed and wrote; the warning is in the table.

LG-15: no upstream wsib_registry/entities activity and no config_version bump since link_wsib's own last completed run — generalizes the pre-existing B3 SKIP. Re-emits the prior run's threshold_updated_at so the NEXT run's config_version diff still has a baseline.
G-12: unlinked_start measured 0 — every wsib_registry row already carries a link. A genuine zero-work completion, distinct from a gated skip (the step ran and measured; nothing was eligible).
Advisory lock 94 is held by another process — a row-derived SKIP summary, never a bare SDK skip with no audit_table.

RLS enabled with 0 policies and the role does not bypass — every statement would affect 0 rows with no error.
A guards.requires precondition with on_missing: "fail" is absent (pg_trgm, a trigram index, or an RLS policy). Refuses before reading anything.

A declared logic variable (T1-T7) resolved outside its bounds under on_invalid: "fail". hoisted_above_gate puts this refusal ABOVE the advisory lock and the ledger gate — the opposite of the pre-conversion order (Commit A / A1 fix).
